Subject: Content-addressable archival + pgvector warm-store probe

Hi Emily, Harper —

Quick note from our side: we're putting together a short sandbox to validate a hybrid retrieval architecture we think will help customers reduce embedding storage costs while keeping tail-latency low. High level: S3-backed content-addressable storage (CAS) for full-document blobs + a lightweight manifest index (per-snapshot) that maps content-address hashes to pgvector entries for a warm-store of recent vectors.

Core questions we'd like to validate in a 4-week probe:
- Can Pinecone/Weaviate accept a manifest-driven connector (manifest lines with object hash, s3 path, content length, chunk offsets) as the source of truth for indexing?
- Operational behavior for diff-based updates: how to efficiently apply snapshot delta (add/remove) without re-ingesting whole indexes?
- Best-effort TTL/eviction coordination between pgvector warm lanes and S3 cold lane (expectation: warm-store ~30d, cold on S3 with lifecycle rules)
- Observability hooks needed for prefix-level reconciliation (error rates, missing object alerts)

Ask: can Pinecone spin up a short-lived connector in a Pinecone sandbox we provide credentials for? Harper / Nimbus — would you run a small scripted ingestion (<=50k docs sample) and help capture WAL/diff behavior for pgvector-based warm stores?

I've attached a draft manifest schema and a tiny sample manifest. Vanessa — can you drive security intake? Ben — can you own the success criteria and metric collection?

If this looks reasonable I propose a kickoff this week and a mutual action plan in Confluence.

Thanks,
Avery

Avery —

Thanks for the clear outline. Pinecone can absolutely run a sandbox connector against a manifest-driven source; we've done similar workflows for object-backed indexes. A couple items up front:
1) Manifest format: your sample looks fine; we'll need a stable unique key per vector (content-hash ok) and a small metadata blob (source_url, last_modified_ts).
2) Delta application: we recommend producing an operation stream (add/remove/touch) rather than snapshot-only ingestion for efficiency — Pinecone supports upserts + deletes via bulk APIs and we can provide a small adapter reference.
3) Consistency/observability: we can emit reconciliation metrics (missing objects, hash mismatches) back to a webhook.

We can accept credentials for a sandbox bucket and test the connector. Timeline: 1 week to stand up adapter, 2 weeks of ingestion, 1 week of joint post-mortem. We'll need a quick security checklist from your team to sign off on temporary creds.

I'll loop in an engineer once we confirm dates.

Cheers,
Emily

Hi all —

Attached: manifest-schema-v1.yaml and sample-s3-manifest.jsonl (small, 2k records) and a preliminary security checklist. Highlights from security side:
- Temporary IAM role with least privilege (ListBucket, GetObject on sample prefix)
- Pre-signed URLs preferred for short-lived object retrieval during ingestion
- No PII in sample set; production will follow DSR/PII redaction rules

Operational notes:
- We'll expose a staging prefix s3://redwood-caddr-test/2026-11/ with object names following content-hash/<original-filename>. We expect manifest lines: content_hash, s3_path, content_len, chunk_count, created_ts, source_id.
- For warm-store behavior we plan to keep a rolling 30-day window in pgvector; older content must be resolvable via manifest -> S3 retrieval.

Ben will own metrics: ingestion throughput, upsert latency, reconciliation error rate, storage delta. Karthik — can you sign off on the pgvector tailing approach (WAL-based vs diff snapshots)?

Vanessa

On Tue, Nov 2, 2026 at 08:22 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi all —
>
> Attached: manifest-schema-v1.yaml and sample-s3-manifest.jsonl ...

Thanks — this looks good. A couple practical observations from the pgvector/broker side based on past pilots:
- WAL tailing can work but often requires tight coupling to the DB engine. For quick probes we recommend a diff-snapshot approach where you produce a small incremental manifest (adds/removes) every 5-15 minutes. That avoids DB-level dependencies and is easier to reconcile in case of missed events.
- Deduping by content-hash is great; ensure you include a stable canonicalization step so semantically equivalent documents map to the same hash (e.g., whitespace normalization, strip markup).
- For long tails, consider a lightweight bloom-filter index per-snapshot to cheaply detect whether an object might exist in cold storage before issuing a GetObject. Saves costs on S3 GETs during reconciliation.

Action items from Nimbus: we'll provide a sample delta-producer script (Python) and a small verifier to run against your staging prefix. ETA: EOD Thursday for the scripts.

Harper
